title: On-call handoff draft - Leo Garcia
content:
Shift: 2026-02-28 09:00 - 2026-03-01 09:00 (PST)
Owner: Leo Garcia
Summary: Quiet shift overall. Two incidents: a transient p50 latency spike for hosted-api route /v1/generate (resolved automatically) and a staging GPU node failure affecting a single Dedicated pool (manual failover executed). No customer-facing outages.

Incidents (brief)
1) HOSTED-API latency spike (2026-02-28 10:45)
   - Symptom: p50 increased ~2x for ~7 minutes on region us-west-2, primarily model: redwood-alpha-3b. Streaming responses slowed, some client timeouts reported.
   - Detection: Alert 'hosted-api-latency-p50-us-west-2' fired in PagerDuty.
   - Mitigation: Smart routing kicked in (fallback to redwood-alpha-3b-quant), traffic gradually shifted; prefix cache warm-up reduced cost of fallback. No rollbacks.
   - Root cause (suspected): Short-lived NVIDIA driver glitch on one serving host combined with a sudden spike in small-batch traffic.
   - Status: Resolved. Follow-up items listed below.

2) DEDICATED pool gpu-node-7 failure (2026-02-28 15:10)
   - Symptom: Node lost registration with autoscaler; jobs in flight retried on other hosts, some inference latencies increased for tenants on that pool for ~12 minutes.
   - Action: Performed manual cordon and drain on node; autoscaler replaced instance. Filed infra issue.
   - Linked ticket: ENG-4521.

Ongoing alerts / things to watch (as of handoff)
- hosted-api-error-rate-us-east-1: marginally elevated, but below pager threshold. Watching for any noise related to new deployment (alpha-3b rollout).
- dedicated-pool-queue-depth: small increase for pool-d-prod during bulk training jobs; autoscaling is currently allowing small bursts.

Temporary procedures / runbook drafts (notes for whoever picks up)
- Quick triage checklist for latency alerts:
  1) Check PagerDuty + Alert details for affected region/model/route.
  2) Look at recent deploys: View last 30 minutes in GitHub Actions / deploy-log.
  3) Check node health in infra dashboard (cpu/gpu temp, memory, driver errors).
  4) If single node implicated, trigger smart-routing fallback for the affected model: Console -> Routing -> Add override to prefer variant -quant for 10m; monitor.
  5) If widespread, consider temporary rate-limit tightening for non-critical routes until stabilization.
  6) Notify SRE slack channel #sre-oncall with one-line summary and link to the alert.

- Temporary failover procedure for Dedicated pool node failure (short-term until infra fix):
  1) Identify failed node in cluster manager.
  2) Cordon node and drain in rolling fashion to avoid overload on remaining nodes.
  3) If autoscaler fails to replace within 10m, escalate to infra oncall (see contacts).
  4) For impacted tenants, trigger graceful capacity burst: Console -> Dedicated -> Pool -> Increase burst capacity to +20% for 15m.
  5) Open a postmortem ticket if customer impact observed.

Operational notes / keyboard shortcuts
- Common dashboards: https://observability.redwood.com/dashboards/hosted-api-latency ; https://observability.redwood.com/dashboards/dedicated-pool-health
- Quick log queries:
  * latency spikes: logs> "route:/v1/generate" | stats p50,p95 by region,model 30m
  * driver/gpu errors: infra> node.* | grep -i nvidia

Escalation contacts (order)
- Primary SRE oncall: Maya Singh (pager)
- Infra lead: Noah Thompson (pager)
- PM / Product owner for hosted-api: Priya Menon (slack)
- Customer Success for impacted customers: Aisha Rahman (email)

Follow-ups / TODOs created during shift
- ENG-4521: Investigate and patch node replacement timing in autoscaler (assigned to infra).
- CONFLUENCE-314: Draft short postmortem template for short-lived latency spikes to capture mitigations faster (assigned to me).
- Add a routing-canary to minimize blast radius when alpha-3b model rollouts happen.

Notes to self / reminders (work-in-progress)
- Draft a small runbook section for "model variant fallback" with exact console steps + CLI commands. Need to include how to revert the override.
- Consider adding an alert that correlates driver errors + latency to reduce false positives.

Misc scratchpad (links & commands)
- Infra replace node command (internal): infractl node replace --id gpu-node-7 
- Rollout history for alpha-3b: https://ci.redwood.com/runs/alpha-3b/last-24h

Ending status: passing off to Maya Singh, asked to keep an eye on hosted-api-error-rate-us-east-1 and the alpha-3b gradual rollout. If anything spikes, follow the quick triage checklist above.

-- Leo
